classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate the two sides independently, reduce 510 degrees using periodicity, select the signed exact values at 300 and 210 degrees, and combine the products to confirm equality.

content.prompt: Show that the relationship $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$ is satisfied when $A=300^\circ$ and $B=210^\circ$.

answer.short:
Both sides equal $\frac12$.

Evaluate each side separately using exact trigonometric values.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\sin(A+B)&=\sin(300^\circ+210^\circ)\\\sin(A+B)&=\sin510^\circ\\\sin(A+B)&=\sin150^\circ\\\sin(A+B)&=\frac12\end{align*}$$$$\begin{align*}\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B&=\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)+\frac12\left(-\frac12\right)\\\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B&=\frac34-\frac14\\\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B&=\frac12\end{align*}$$Both sides equal $\frac12$, so the relationship is satisfied.
